source.text: A lumped body started at its steady state T_b + q'/(h A) and then cooled less and less well: the same ODE through a film history that falls in a straight line over ten seconds. Heat capacity per metre 206.404 J/m/K, outer surface 29.8451 mm2/mm. The pin warms monotonically, so the largest peak is the value at 40 s: 682.7699 K from 611.1688 K. The tolerance is 1 % of the rise, fixed before any run (first-order step error 0.4 % at most, the lumped approximation, the 0.05 s the solver applies the new film value late).
source.check: Second method: FEED's independent finite-volume solution of the full pin with the history (src/core/transientFv.ts, tests/transientFvBoundary.test.ts, exact lumped solutions) and the real solver through tests/seedOracleBoundaryHistory.test.ts; the history is written to OFFBEAT as timeDependentAxialProfileHTC and judged by FEED's own cross-check in docs/boundary-history.md.

coverage.domain: synthetic pin with a conductivity of 400 W/m/K and a heat capacity of 3 MJ/m3/K (Biot about 0.01), 1 kW/m started from its own steady state at a film coefficient of 3000 W/m2/K, coolant 600 K, the film coefficient decaying linearly to 300 between 5 and 15 s
